_note: 懐石・会席・精進・弁当（日本の構えた食事の型）の系譜。品目ハブ（/en/eat/kaiseki/）の横並び表と、各系譜ページがここから描く。出典は docs/research/kaiseki-shojin-bento-2026-10-11.md と各系譜ページの sources。tea は茶懐石と会席を1ページで扱う。planned の行の era は、系譜ページを書いて出典が付くまで「—」のまま（記憶の年号を出さない）。本膳・弁当はメモに素材があるが系譜ページ未執筆
name: Kaiseki and the formal meal

origin.place: The tea gathering; banquet kaiseki at restaurants
origin.era: Tea kaiseki completed in the Momoyama period (farm ministry)

cells.occasion: Tea: a light meal before the tea. Banquet: a meal for drinking sake
cells.structure: Tea: one tray, one soup and three dishes, then dishes for sake. Banquet: many dishes, order set by the cook
cells.rice: Tea: first, with the soup. Banquet: near the end
cells.marker: Tea kaiseki ends with matcha; the banquet is what restaurants now usually call kaiseki

origin.era: About 700 years ago, or the Kamakura period (sources differ)

cells.occasion: Monks’ food as part of training; separately, hospitality for temple visitors
cells.structure: Monks: one soup, one dish. Hospitality: trays in the honzen style (Kōya lunches of two or three trays)
cells.marker: No meat or fish; tofu, yuba and fu; kombu and dried shiitake for stock

cells.structure: From a first tray (the honzen) up to a fifth
cells.marker: Said by Kyoto city’s education board to be the base of formal Japanese cooking

origin.place: Food carried out: theatre, travel, tea gatherings
origin.era: Reached Kyoto from China at the end of the 1300s (farm ministry)

cells.occasion: Theatre intervals, rail travel, the simplified meal at a tea gathering
cells.structure: Rice and several side dishes in one box; the Shōkadō box has four compartments
cells.marker: Makunouchi from the theatre; Shōkadō from a ryōtei in 1937
